title: NorthStar Labs PLG self-serve fit + hosting options
summary: Intro discovery for NorthStar evaluating Redwood self-serve API vs Dedicated/Private. Discussed time-to-first-token (TTFT) playbook, free credits, security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and pilot success metrics. Agreed to send security pack, pricing bands, and spin up a free-credits sandbox; schedule a 1-hour benchmark demo next week.

transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood - AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood - SE), Emma Patel (NorthStar - CTO), Jonah Price (NorthStar - Lead ML), Samir Khan (NorthStar - DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Discussed quickstart path and hosted vs private fit; security and pilot metrics.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, AE for the account, and Carlos is our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:07] Emma Patel: Hey Maya, good thanks. Excited to chat — we are trying to figure out whether Redwood's self-serve API is the right first step or if we need to jump straight into a dedicated/reserved setup.
[00:18] Carlos Ruiz: Great, thanks Emma. We'll run through TTFT — time-to-first-token — playbook, free credits, and some security fit questions. But first, can you give a quick picture of your stack and what you're trying to build?
[00:30] Jonah Price: Sure. We're building a conversational assistant embedded in our analytics dashboard. Low latency is important for UI flows, but we're also cost-sensitive since we expect a lot of cheap queries. Right now we're evaluating prototypes on CloudAICo and a few OSS models.
[00:45] Samir Khan: From infra side, we're containerized on AWS with VPCs, and there are strict data residency controls for EU customers. Also, infosec will want SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Perfect, that's the core of the conversation. For PLG/self-serve we usually recommend spinning up a free-credits sandbox and running a quick TTFT path — get to first call within a day or two. If you need predictable throughput we can discuss Dedicated or Private later.
[01:12] Emma Patel: When you say "free-credits sandbox", what's the scope? Is it the hosted API only?
[01:18] Carlos Ruiz: It's hosted by default — you'll get an API key, sample workspace, example prompts, and limited credits you can use for benchmarks. We also provide sample benchmark scripts for latency and throughput. If you later want to test Dedicated we can set up a short reserved pilot but that usually requires an agreement.
[01:34] Jonah Price: Can we run a KV cache / prefix cache test? One of our big cost wins is prefix caching on long docs.
[01:40] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, absolutely. We have KV cache behaviors and sample setups. Note that in some transcripts folks call it "K-V cash" in notes, so apologies for the weird phrasing in auto transcripts.
[01:49] Samir Khan: For EU data, we can't send raw PII to hosted endpoints without a contract. Is Private deploy (VPC/on-prem) viable for a pilot?
[01:58] Maya Chen: Private is doable but longer lead time. Typical path we've seen: start hosted self-serve to validate UX and prompts (fast TTFT), then migrate to Dedicated or Private for compliance and throughput guarantees. For EU PII you can also apply data-filtering / tokenization client-side during the PLG phase as a stop-gap.
[02:14] Emma Patel: What's the typical TTFT in your playbook? We want the product manager to see an actual call in 48 hours ideally.
[02:20] Carlos Ruiz: For basic generation/chat, TTFT is often < 24 hours for engineers who have an API key. For your use-case with caching and integration into an analytics UI, plan for 24-72 hours to get a meaningful demo. We'll help with a quickstart that includes curl, JS SDK examples, and a small script you can paste into your app.
[02:37] Jonah Price: Any gotchas on auth? We use Okta — SAML SSO is a blocker for some dashboards.
[02:43] Maya Chen: SSO for the Redwood Console / account is supported via SAML/Okta. For API-level auth we use API keys and you can integrate with your secrets manager (KMS/HSM). We'll include the SSO onboarding doc in the security pack.
[02:55] Samir Khan: Audit logs — can we get token-level logs and per-route latency?
[03:01] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, Console has token-level consumption, per-model latency breakdown, and request traces. For Private deployments, audit/export logs can be pushed to your SIEM. We'll share screenshots in the pack.
[03:12] Emma Patel: What about SOC 2? We need to show infosec something quick for the pilot.
[03:16] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — we'll attach the attestation and the summary in the security package. If you need extra paperwork we can coordinate via our security team.
[03:26] Jonah Price: Cost question — if we go hosted, what's the cost delta for 5k queries/day at 512 tokens vs running our own inferencing?
[03:33] Carlos Ruiz: It depends on model selection and batching. We usually recommend a smaller encoder-decoder or quantized model for cost-sensitive high-volume traffic. Our Optimize toolkit gives batching suggestions — many customers see 30-50% unit cost reduction by enabling prefix caching and continuous batching. We'll include a rough cost model in the follow-up.
[03:52] Samir Khan: If we need reserved throughput, how does Dedicated pricing and SLAs look?
[03:57] Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable throughput and an SLA. Pricing is monthly commit-based; we can share tiered options. Typical pilot for teams your size is a 3-month reserved pool with burst capacity.
[04:09] Emma Patel: We have a hard latency goal — 95th percentile under 300ms for short prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?
[04:16] Carlos Ruiz: 300ms 95th is aggressive but possible for smaller models and with caching + edge routing. Hosted regions and model selection matter; if you need strict 300ms SLOs, Dedicated or Private with colocated GPUs gives more control. For PLG proof of concept, start with hosted to validate functional metrics, then run a short benchmark with our runtime to see if hosted hits your SLO.
[04:39] Jonah Price: Can you walk through an example TTFT checklist? We want to share this with PMs.
[04:44] Carlos Ruiz: Sure — short checklist: 1) Sign up, get API keys and free credits; 2) Run our sample prompt set against a small model to validate responses; 3) Run latency/throughput benchmark (we'll provide script); 4) Integrate SDK into UI demo; 5) Evaluate cost with caching and adjust model/quantization; 6) Decide on Dedicated/Private if compliance/performance needs require it.
[05:07] Emma Patel: Sounds good. Who owns step 3 and 5?
[05:12] Maya Chen: We'll own the benchmark scripts and the initial sandbox. Jonah, if you share the prompt set we'll plug it into the script.
[05:20] Jonah Price: Okay I'll share a sample of 50 prompts covering short UI utterances and longer context summaries.
[05:27] Samir Khan: One more ops question — for Private installs, how are upgrades handled? We have concerns about patch windows.
[05:33] Carlos Ruiz: Private deployments are coordinated with your ops team. We support staged rollouts and can run upgrades during agreed maintenance windows. We also provide a private control plane if you want to keep the orchestration inside your VPC.
[05:45] Emma Patel: Any red flags from your side about our timeline? We're hoping to show a demo to execs in three weeks.
[05:50] Maya Chen: Three weeks for a demo is reasonable if you start with hosted self-serve and keep the scope narrow. If you want production-grade latency/residency guarantees in that time it's tougher; Dedicated/Private setup takes longer. We'll propose a minimal viable demo scope in the follow-up.
[06:05] Jonah Price: About integrations — we use Redis for session state. Will Redwood's session/KV cache play nice or do we need to swap?
[06:12] Carlos Ruiz: You can keep Redis for app state; Redwood's KV/prefix caching is at the inference layer. They complement each other. We'll document recommended patterns.
[06:20] Samir Khan: For EU data, if we mask PII on client side, is hosted acceptable for the pilot?
[06:26] Maya Chen: Masking is a common approach for pilots. We'll include guidance on redaction and tokenization as part of the security pack. If infosec needs to see flow diagrams, we can produce those.
[06:36] Emma Patel: Great. Can you also include a simple runbook for rollback if model quality regresses? That's a concern for product.
[06:43] Carlos Ruiz: Yes — Redwood console supports rollouts, canary deploys, and automatic fallback policies. We'll include a one-page runbook: steps to rollback, how to rollback model version, and how to set up automatic fallback to a safe model.
[06:59] Maya Chen: Quick question for Jonah — what metric will define pilot success? Response quality? Latency? Cost per 1k calls?
[07:06] Jonah Price: Primary: functional correctness on a 50-prompt eval set (target > 85% pass rate). Secondary: 95th pct latency < 600ms for initial pilot and cost per 1k calls under our internal threshold.
[07:18] Maya Chen: Cool. We'll align the sandbox and benchmark to those targets.
[07:23] Carlos Ruiz: Side note — if you want to try a tiny quantized model to start, we can recommend one that balances latency and quality. Often customers start with a quantized 7B variant for UI flows.
[07:33] Emma Patel: That sounds reasonable. Any compliance gotchas if we ingest logs? We need to be careful about storing chat transcripts.
[07:41] Maya Chen: You can configure retention and disable logging for sensitive routes. For Private/Dedicated, full control over storage. We'll include retention config options in security docs.
[07:55] Samir Khan: About pricing — is there an easy calculator or example spreadsheet?
[07:59] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we'll attach a cost-model spreadsheet with assumptions: tokens, model, batch sizes, and caching effects. That should make it concrete for finance.
[08:09] Emma Patel: OK, unless there are more questions..
[08:12] Jonah Price: A couple quick clarifications: 1) Can we pin model versions? 2) Are streaming responses supported for UI?
[08:18] Carlos Ruiz: 1) Yes, you can pin versions and rollout safely. 2) Streaming is supported via the SDK and REST streaming — good for progressive UI render.
[08:26] Samir Khan: Do you support private key rotation with KMS?
[08:29] Maya Chen: Yes, KMS integrations and HSM options are available on Private and through managed integrations on Hosted. We'll include key rotation docs.
[08:37] Emma Patel: Great. Let's recap and next steps.
[08:40] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to provision hosted free-credits sandbox and invite NorthStar; send security pack (SOC2, SSO, KMS, logs); share cost-model spreadsheet; Carlos to prepare benchmark script and suggested model/config; Jonah to share 50-prompt eval set and target SLOs.
[08:59] Jonah Price: I'll drop the prompt set in the shared folder by Friday.
[09:03] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll send calendar invite for the benchmark/demo next Tuesday 2025-10-07 10:00 PT. Any final questions?
[09:11] Emma Patel: No, that covers it. Thanks everyone.
[09:13] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the materials. Bye!

Auto-generated action items (end): Maya to send security pack; Carlos to prepare scripts; Jonah to share prompts.
